metaDescription: Five rechargeable cordless floor lamps compared on battery size, run time, adjustable height and water resistance for rooms without a nearby outlet.
introParagraphs: A cordless floor lamp solves the oddly common problem of a dark spot far from an outlet, whether that is a reading chair, a patio table or a hallway where a cord would be a trip hazard. The five lamps here run on built-in batteries, and they differ most in battery size and in how well they handle being moved. The O'Bright Sandy lists up to 60 hours per charge and an IP44 water-resistant build, while the MOKOQI and LGMCF both carry 7800mAh batteries and the NBPLUS and QiMH use 5000mAh and 5400mAh packs.

The spread in height and shape matters as much as battery capacity. The O'Bright has a weighted base with five customizable heights and a head that detaches as a carry light, the LGMCF reaches up to 63 inches or 45.27 inches with one pole removed, and the NBPLUS has a flexible gooseneck with two heights. The QiMH is the odd one out because its battery sits in a rechargeable bulb controlled by a remote.

We evaluated each lamp on battery capacity and listed run time, how easily its height and head can be adjusted, how simple the controls are, and how well it suits being carried, based on product specs and buyer feedback. For active adults we favored lamps with physical or touch dimming and clear charging behavior over those that depend on a remote you might misplace.

products.name: O'Bright Sandy Cordless LED Floor Lamp

specList.label: Portability
specList.value: Head works as a carry light

products.description:
The O'Bright Sandy is the most complete cordless lamp in this group. It lists up to 60 hours per full charge, which is long enough that charging becomes a weekly rather than a nightly habit. A weighted base supports five customizable heights, and the lamp head can stand alone as a carry light.

It is also the only pick with a stated IP44 rating, which means it is protected against splashes from any direction and can withstand rain and water spray. That makes it the one to choose for a covered porch or patio as well as a living room. The tradeoff is that it sits in a higher cost tier, and the listing gives no lumen figure, so it is a practical glow rather than a proven task light.

A battery indicator light shows red while charging and turns off when the lamp is full, which is simple enough for anyone to read at a glance. Compared with the MOKOQI's 7800mAh battery and 8 to 15 hour run time, the O'Bright is the better choice if you want far longer between charges. We rank it first for the combination of run time, water resistance and a carry-around head.
products.bestFor: Indoor and covered outdoor use with long battery life
pros: Up to 60 hours per full charge
IP44 rating handles splashes and rain spray
Five customizable heights on a weighted base
Head detaches as a carry light
cons: Higher cost tier than most picks
Splash rated, so not for full submersion

products.name: MOKOQI 15W Rechargeable Cordless Floor Lamp
products.description:
The MOKOQI is a light-bar style cordless lamp with a 7800mAh battery and a 15W LED output. The listing states 8 to 15 hours of working time per charge, depending on brightness. Three color temperatures are available, so you can switch between warm and cooler light as the task changes.

Control is by touch, with a short press switching color temperature and a long press adjusting brightness from 5 to 100 percent, and a memory function recalls your last setting. The advantage is smooth dimming that suits aging eyes, because you can fine-tune the light at low levels. The limitation is that touch controls can be less forgiving than a physical button for some people, and the run time depends heavily on brightness.

It is a good fit for a reading chair where a cord is inconvenient, and recharging is a matter of plugging it in overnight when needed. Compared with the O'Bright's 60 hour claim, the MOKOQI has a shorter run time, but its light-bar design delivers brighter, more even illumination in a living room. It is also much easier to use than the QiMH because everything is on the lamp, with no remote to keep track of.
products.bestFor: A bright, evenly lit reading chair
pros: 7800mAh battery with 8 to 15 hours of use
Three color temperatures to match the task
Smooth touch dimming from 5 to 100 percent
Memory function recalls last setting
cons: Run time drops at full brightness
Touch controls may suit some users less

products.name: LGMCF 15W Cordless Gooseneck Floor Lamp

specList.label: Height
specList.value: Up to 63 inches, 45.27 inches with one pole removed

products.description:
The LGMCF pairs a 7800mAh battery with a flexible gooseneck and 15W output. The gooseneck bends 360 degrees and the head rotates 180 degrees, so you can aim light onto a page, a craft table or a keyboard. It arrives fully assembled and reaches up to 63 inches, or 45.27 inches with one pole removed.

That two-height design makes it flexible, because the taller setting works beside a standing chair and the shorter one suits a side table. Touch control gives three color temperatures and stepless dimming. The tradeoff is that a gooseneck can droop over time and needs a firm hand to reposition, and the brief gives no run time figure to compare with the MOKOQI.

The lamp stores easily because you can remove a pole section, and it recharges through a cable rather than a stand. Compared with the NBPLUS's 5000mAh battery and two heights, the LGMCF offers more capacity and a taller reach. It is the lamp we would choose for a crafter or reader who changes seat position often.
products.bestFor: Readers and crafters who need to aim the light
pros: Fully assembled out of the box
Reaches 63 inches or 45.27 inches
360 degree gooseneck with a rotating head
7800mAh battery with touch dimming
cons: No run time listed to compare

products.name: NBPLUS Cordless Portable Floor Lamp
products.description:
The NBPLUS is a lightweight cordless lamp with a 5000mAh battery and a 360 degree flexible gooseneck. It offers two adjustable heights and three color modes, warm, natural and cool. Stepless dimming with touch control lets you set the brightness precisely.

Its selling point is portability, since the listing positions it for outdoor use and everyday movement from room to room. The smaller battery is the tradeoff, because it holds less charge than the 7800mAh MOKOQI and LGMCF, so expect to recharge more often. The listing also does not give a lumen figure.

Setup is quick with minimal assembly, and recharging uses a cable. It sits at a lower mid-range cost tier, which makes it a sensible choice if you want a gooseneck lamp without paying for a larger battery. Compared with the LGMCF, you give up capacity and some height in exchange for a lighter, simpler lamp.
products.bestFor: Light carrying and occasional outdoor use
pros: Lightweight and easy to move
Flexible 360 degree gooseneck
Two heights and three color modes
Lower mid-range cost tier

products.name: QiMH Rechargeable Bulb Cordless Floor Lamp
products.description:
The QiMH takes a different approach, with a rechargeable bulb included inside a standing lamp. The 5400mAh battery powers three color temperatures and an RGB mode, and the remote controls nine RGB colors. Stepless dimming and two light modes, smooth and flash, are also listed.

Three timer modes provide auto-off, which is useful at a bedside or in a guest room. The tradeoff is dependence on a remote, which is easy to misplace, and the flash mode and color options add complexity that many adults will not use. It is also the highest cost pick here, so you pay a premium for the remote and bulb system.

Because the battery sits in the bulb, replacing it means replacing the bulb rather than the lamp, which is a useful ownership detail to consider. Compared with the O'Bright, it lacks a water-resistance rating and run time claim, but the timer and remote make it more convenient for a bedroom. It suits people who want to control a lamp from a bed or chair without getting up.
products.bestFor: Remote control from a bed or sofa
pros: Remote controls colors, timer and dimming
Three auto-off timer modes
Rechargeable bulb included
Three color temperatures plus RGB
cons: Highest cost tier of the five
Flash and RGB modes add complexity

buyingCriteria.explanation: Battery size in mAh is the first number to check, but it only tells part of the story. The MOKOQI and LGMCF both carry 7800mAh, the QiMH 5400mAh and the NBPLUS 5000mAh, while the O'Bright lists up to 60 hours per charge. The MOKOQI states 8 to 15 hours depending on brightness, which shows how much run time falls at full output. Choose a lamp with at least a full evening of use at your usual brightness.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Brightness at low and high settings
buyingCriteria.explanation: A cordless lamp trades battery life for brightness, so a lamp that dims smoothly lets you stretch a charge. The MOKOQI and LGMCF both offer stepless dimming, with the MOKOQI listing a 5 to 100 percent range. Guides suggest 400 to 800 lumens on a reading surface and that aging eyes often need more, so a wide dimming range helps. Since several of these listings give no lumen figure, favor lamps with fine dimming.

Cordless lamps often move outdoors, where splashes matter. The O'Bright is the only pick with a stated IP44 rating, protecting against splashes from any direction. The other four list no rating, so keep them indoors or under cover. An IP44 rating does not mean the lamp can sit in standing water.

A good cordless lamp should reach the page without being moved. The LGMCF reaches 63 inches and drops to 45.27 inches with a pole removed, the O'Bright offers five heights, and the NBPLUS has two. Goosenecks and swivel heads let you aim the light at a page without moving the lamp, which matters when you are reading. Check that the neck holds its position firmly.

Controls decide whether you use a lamp daily. Physical buttons on the pole generally outperform touch sensors, which can fail with dry skin or poor circulation. The MOKOQI, LGMCF and NBPLUS use touch, and the QiMH uses a remote. If touch is difficult for you, prefer a lamp with an obvious button or a remote you can keep near your chair.

Charging behavior is the hidden cost of a cordless lamp. The O'Bright's indicator turns red while charging and off when full, a clear cue. Charge the lamp somewhere out of walking paths and route the cable away from where you walk. A lamp with a small battery such as the NBPLUS will need to be charged more often, so plan a spot near an outlet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and run time
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated battery sizes, from the NBPLUS's 5000mAh to the 7800mAh packs in the MOKOQI and LGMCF, along with run time claims like the O'Bright's 60 hours. We noted that run time depends on brightness. The picks with clear run time figures scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at height ranges and head movement, including the LGMCF's 63 inch reach, the O'Bright's five heights and the NBPLUS's two. A lamp that aims light where you need it scores better for reading. We also checked buyer feedback about gooseneck sag.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control simplicity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared touch controls, remote control and indicator lights. The QiMH relies on a remote, while the MOKOQI, LGMCF and NBPLUS use touch. Lamps with clear, forgiving controls scored higher for our audience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered weight, base design and weather protection. The O'Bright's weighted base and IP44 rating make it the strongest and most versatile, while the NBPLUS is the lightest and the most basic in build. This comparison shaped our ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed features against relative price tier, from the O'Bright at a mid tier to the QiMH at the highest. A higher tier needed a clear benefit such as run time, a rating or a remote with timers.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Hallway or Dark Corner Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a stable base, long run time and a lamp that is easy to switch on in the dark. A cord-free lamp removes a trip hazard in a hallway, but a tall slim lamp can tip if bumped. Place it against a wall.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The O'Bright's weighted base and 60 hour run time make it the best fit for a hallway. The MOKOQI is a strong alternative for a bright corner.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want long run time and weather protection, as the O'Bright offers, or a remote with timers like the QiMH. These features cost more but add convenience.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You move the lamp rarely and charge it often. The NBPLUS at a lower mid-range tier covers the basics.

faq.q: How long does a cordless floor lamp last on one charge?
faq.a: It depends on brightness and battery size. The O'Bright lists up to 60 hours, while the MOKOQI lists 8 to 15 hours. Running at lower brightness extends the time significantly.

faq.q: Which cordless lamp is best for reading?
faq.a: The MOKOQI offers 15W output with smooth dimming from 5 to 100 percent and a 7800mAh battery. The LGMCF is better if you need to aim the light with a gooseneck. Both let you set the brightness precisely.

faq.q: Can I use a cordless lamp outdoors?
faq.a: Only the O'Bright lists a water-resistance rating, IP44, which handles splashes and rain spray. The other four have no stated rating, so use them under cover. Bring any lamp inside during heavy rain.

faq.q: Do cordless lamps need special bulbs?
faq.a: Most use built-in LEDs, but the QiMH uses a rechargeable bulb with a battery inside. Replacing that bulb replaces the battery too. Check this before you buy.

faq.q: Is a cordless lamp as bright as a plug-in one?
faq.a: Usually it is not, because battery power limits output. The 15W lamps here are comparable to a modest plug-in lamp. If you need strong task light, check lumens first.

faq.q: How do I make the battery last longer?
faq.a: Use lower brightness and a warm setting when possible. Recharge before the battery is completely empty. Store the lamp with a partial charge if you will not use it for a long time.
